title: 2016-17 — Webster & Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered the stated issue "No" and denied the complaint. It held that Heritage Presbytery's September 10, 2016 motion did not impinge on the session's authority or the session/congregation's election prerogatives and did not violate the Constitution. The SJC did not rule on the Ullrey complaint's merits or on whether presbytery discussions would disqualify presbyters, because that complaint was not before presbytery.
first_summary: Did Heritage Presbytery err by cautioning a session and requesting postponement of a candidate's election or ordination while a complaint about his qualifications was pending? The SJC denied the complaint. It reasoned that the presbytery only gave advice, not an order, and that the session could disregard it. It also noted that BCO 43-2 did not prohibit presbyters from discussing a complaint not yet before them.
summary: Did Heritage Presbytery err by cautioning a session and requesting that it postpone a candidate's election or ordination while a complaint about his qualifications was pending? The SJC said no and denied the complaint. The motion was advice, not an act for or requirement imposed on the session; the session could disregard it, and BCO 43-2 does not bar presbyters from discussing matters related to a complaint not yet before them. The SJC left undecided whether such discussions would disqualify presbyters, since the Ullrey complaint never reached presbytery.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2016-17, Webster & Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery, SJC decision on complaint dated Aug. 30, 2017; reported in 46th GA (2018) at source lines 1–5, 13–15. The proposed opinion was revised and approved by the SJC on a roll call (lines 132–136); no separate opinions are noted.
evidence_notes.dispute: Heritage Presbytery appointed an ad interim committee, received its report and addendum, and on Sept. 10, 2016 passed a motion cautioning New Covenant Session and requesting postponement of a candidate's consideration/election/ordination until an Ullrey complaint was resolved. Webster and Fowler complained; HP denied on Nov. 12, 2016; the GA complaint became SJC 2016-17 (lines 19–73). The stated issue appears at lines 77–100.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC judgment: "No." (line 104). Reasoning: HP did not act for or require the session to act; it provided advice the session could ignore. HP properly recognized the Ullrey Complaint was not before it; BCO 43-2 bars parties from circularizing, not presbyters from discussing related matters. The advice did not impinge lower-court authority or election prerogatives and did not violate the Constitution. Complaint denied (lines 106–130).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC expressly left undecided whether presbytery discussions could render presbyters ineligible to rule on a complaint, because the Ullrey complaint was never before presbytery (lines 116–120). The opinion was edited/revised and adopted by roll call, with no dissent noted (lines 132–136).
